tagline: We make a number for every game. We bet the ones where the market's wrong.

games.take: Both teams are 4-2 and the market has sat on Bears -3 all week, so the price on the key number is the whole story. New England will be without both starting guards (Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown) plus CB Carlton Davis III, with two backup corners already ruled out — a reshuffled interior against a Chicago front with 17 sacks on a short week is the sharpest pressure point in the game. Caleb Williams returned from a three-game hamstring absence last week and went 30-of-36 against Atlanta. Chicago averages 160.7 rushing yards per game, but without Kyle Monangai (out again) that number has cratered to 89.5. No true edge at -3 against our fair line — but if you're picking a side, the patched-up Patriots line vs the Chicago pass rush is the reason to lean the home favorite.
games.title: Thursday Night Football

games.matchup: James Madison Dukes @ Appalachian State Mountaineers
games.take: The 7-0 Dukes are 4-0 in Sun Belt play and 3-0 on the road, averaging 42.9 points per game behind a physical run game (George Pettaway, 767 yards, 7 TDs). The advanced ratings back them hard — roughly a 17-point gap in SP+ before home field. App State's offense is the problem: the Mountaineers managed three points at home against Old Dominion, QB Malachi Singleton's ankle status is uncertain, both lead backs are questionable, and two defensive linemen are out. The total dropped from 57.5 to 56.5 despite nearly all the money on the Over — reverse line movement worth respecting. No true edge: Pinnacle has pushed to -12.5 past the -10.5/-11.5 consensus. Lean JMU because the rating gap and the QB uncertainty are real, but the number has moved away from us.
games.title: JMU at App State

games.take: Liberty has won five straight, four by at least 16 points, and owns top-20 EPA marks in every offensive category. QB Deshawn Purdie has eight touchdowns without an interception, and the Flames average 223 rushing yards per game (15th nationally) against a Kennesaw State defense that ranks 118th in passing EPA and havoc rate. But the Owls have lost their last three by a combined seven points — they're competitive, just unable to finish — and they own this series recently (wins in 2024 and last November). No true edge at -9.5 against our fair line. Lean Liberty because the talent and EPA gaps are too wide for a full 60 minutes, but the one-score-loss streak means the dog is live.
games.title: Liberty at Kennesaw State

games.take: Memphis has the more explosive offense by a mile — QB Marcus Stokes leads the conference with 18 touchdown passes, RB Jaylin Carter leads it with 780 rushing yards — but the Tigers are coming off a 31-17 loss at Tulane where they turned it over six times, and this spread has already moved from -9.5 to -10.5 on all-Tigers money. ECU has covered seven of its last ten against Memphis, won the last three meetings, and five of its six games this season have gone Under the total. The Pirates' offense is limited (655 passing yards for Emory Williams), but their defense has allowed 27 or fewer in four straight regulation games. No true edge on the side. Lean the Under 54: ECU's pace and red-zone limitations make it hard for them to do their share of the scoring.
games.title: ECU at Memphis
games.venue: Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium, Memphis TN

games.take: Cleveland opens its season in Philadelphia, where the new-look 76ers are 1-0 after grinding out a 106-100 win at the Knicks on Tuesday — the first look at LeBron James, Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid sharing a floor, with Maxey dropping 28. The injury report is the whole story: Jarrett Allen is questionable with a knee issue, and the market moved from -2.5 to -3.5 on his uncertainty. If he plays, Cleveland getting +3.5 is the best number on the board; if he sits, the move is roughly fair. The Cavs kept Mitchell, Harden, Mobley and added Peyton Watson, and they posted a +4.1 net rating last season against -0.1 for Philly. No true edge either way — lean Cavaliers +3.5, but wait for Allen's status before anything touches real money.
games.title: Cavs at 76ers

games.take: Denver opens its season in the league's toughest road building against a Thunder team that opened with a 116-104 win at San Antonio on Tuesday behind Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's 32. The Thunder are co-title favorites for a reason, but this is the classic letdown spot: emotional season opener Tuesday, now a home favorite laying 8.5 on the second leg of a week-one back-to-back-adjacent stretch while a fresh Denver team with a full offseason walks in. There's no edge against our fair line — OKC is priced like the powerhouse it is. Lean Nuggets +8.5 because early-season road dogs getting the best number (FanDuel and Fanatics deal +8; Pinnacle's 8.5 is the market high) is a structurally sound spot, and the Thunder's pace can just as easily produce a late backdoor as a blowout.
games.title: Nuggets at Thunder
